Cooking Adventure

With this early AI powered prototype, children create their own cooking adventure story starring themselves and their magic animal, with age-appropriate recipes to cook alongside an adult.

An AI project at Julius-Maximilians-Universität Würzburg

My Role

  • Choose your character, magical friend & recipe
  • Read your personalized cooking adventure story
  • Cook the recipe together!

The Need

Cooking is still largely seen as an activity for adults, with most traditional recipes designed exclusively for them. Including children in the cooking process offers numerous benefits.

  • Children develop a positive relationship with food and improve their skills and self-efficacy.
  • At the same time, parents benefit from shared, high-quality time in the kitchen, reduced mealtime stress, and an opportunity to inspire healthy habits through creativity and collaboration.

The Goal

The aim of this project was to develop an initial Flowrabbit prototype using AI flows, enabling children to generate personalized cooking stories that inspire curiosity and intrinsic motivation for cooking together.

Flowrabbit is a no-code platform that lets companies build and share custom GenAI tools and workflows by connecting existing AI services and models.

Research

  • Children’s involvement in food preparation is linked with healthier dietary patterns.
    Cooking together fosters autonomy, skill development, and better family dynamics.

    Raber, M., Hooper, M., Hughes, S., & Wood, A. (2022). Cooking with Kids: A Preliminary Conceptual Model of Child Involvement in Home Food Preparation and Diet Quality. Current Developments in Nutrition, 6, 859.
    https://doi.org/10.1093/cdn/nzac065.043

  • Guidelines for designing age-appropriate cooking intervention programmes for including children in cooking activities at home.

    Dean, M., O'Kane, C., Issartel, J., McCloat, A., Mooney, E., Gaul, D., Wolfson, J.A. & Lavelle, F. (2021). Guidelines for designing age-appropriate cooking interventions for children: the development of evidence-based cooking skill recommendations for children, using a multidisciplinary approach. Appetite, 161, 105125.
    https://doi.org/10.1016/j.appet.2021.105125

  • Fairytale-like stories with appropriate narratives about food can have a strong and lasting effect on the healthy food choices of preschool children.

    Zahedi, A., Katembu, S., Sind, S. M., Sommer, U., Kimamo, C., & Sommer, W. (2025). The impact of a fairytale-like story on the food choices of preschool children. Appetite, 206, 107839.
    https://doi.org/10.1016/j.appet.2024.107839

Target Group

Children, ages 3-12 supported by an adult during use

Motor skills: large buttons and simple interactions for limited fine motor control
Cognitive development: age-appropriate language, visual aids, engaging interface design
Child protection: strict limitations in generated output, no external links or unsafe content

AI Logic

First Draft for AI Flow

  • LLM generates story from user input
  • Image AI generates a picture based on the generated story

Second Draft AI Flow

  • Image AI generating images of meals as a proposition, user can accept or change them (this feature had to be discarded because the image generation is not yet reliable enough)
